'''''Hieracium amplexicaule''''', commonly known as '''sticky hawkweed''', is a [[perennial]] [[herb]] belonging to the family [[Asteraceae]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hieracium amplexicaule L. articles - Encyclopedia of Life |url=http://prod.eol.org/pages/6218999/articles |access-date=2024-12-11 |website=prod.eol.org}}</ref> This species is native to certain regions of [[Europe]] and has been introduced to other parts of the world, where it is considered a [[Introduced species|xenophyte]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Verloove |first1=Filip |last2=Tison |first2=Jean-Marc |title=On the genuine identity of Hieracium amplexicaule (Asteraceae) in Belgium and neighboring territories |journal=Dumortiera |date=5 December 2019 |volume=115 |pages=50–54 |doi=10.5281/zenodo.3553694 }}</ref>

== Botanical description ==
''Hieracium amplexicaule'' is classified as a [[Subshrub|chamaephyte]], a type of perennial plant with [[Regeneration (biology)|regenerative]] buds located above ground level. It typically grows as a low, [[woody plant]] or [[Succulent plant|succulent]], not exceeding 30 cm in height.<ref>{{cite web |title=Hieracium amplexicaule |url=https://floraveg.eu/taxon/overview/Hieracium%20amplexicaule |access-date=11 December 2024 |website=FloraVeg.eu}}</ref> The plant's common name, sticky hawkweed, likely refers to its glandular, adhesive surfaces.

One of the distinctive features of ''H.'' amplexicaule is its stem-clasping leaves, as suggested by its specific epithet "amplexicaule", which means "stem-clasping" in [[Latin]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hieracium amplexicaule L. {{!}} Plants of the World Online {{!}} Kew Science |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:214716-1 |access-date=2024-12-11 |website=Plants of the World Online |language=en}}</ref>

== Distribution and habitat ==
''Hieracium amplexicaule'' has been documented in various European countries. In [[Belgium]], it has been known to occur in the surroundings of [[Tongeren]] since at least 1867. It has also been recorded in neighboring territories, such as near [[Maastricht]] in [[Netherlands|the Netherlands]].

== Reproduction and biology ==
Like other members of the genus [[Hieracium]], ''H. amplexicaule'' is a facultative [[Apomixis|apomict]], meaning it can reproduce both [[Sexual reproduction|sexually]] and [[Asexual reproduction|asexually]]. A single one of its [[ovule]]s can undergo both sexual and asexual [[megagametogenesis]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=van Baarlen |first1=Peter |last2=Verduijn |first2=Marije |last3=van Dijk |first3=Peter J |title=What can we learn from natural apomicts? |journal=Trends in Plant Science |date=February 1999 |volume=4 |issue=2 |pages=43–44 |doi=10.1016/S1360-1385(98)01367-3 |bibcode=1999TPS.....4...43V |quote=The inheritance of apomixis in aposporous Hieracium subgenus Pilosella (Asteraceae) was comparable to Ranunculus. Hieracium is a facultative apomict that can have both sexual and asexual megagametogenesis in one ovule. }}</ref>

== Conservation and ecological impact ==
As an introduced species in some regions, ''Hieracium amplexicaule'' may have [[Ecology|ecological]] implications for native [[flora]]. However, detailed studies on its environmental impact and [[conservation status]] are limited. Further research is needed to fully understand its role in various ecosystems and its potential effects on [[biodiversity]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hieracium amplexicaule L. |url=https://www.gbif.org/species/3136320 |access-date=2024-12-11 |website=www.gbif.org |language=en}}</ref>
